children.text: Many people assume that traveling is necessarily tied to large sums of money. In reality, there are countless destinations where you can have an unforgettable experience even on a small budget. This blog will help you find the cheapest and most popular countries, where prices are affordable and the impressions are unique.

With its pleasant islands and enchanting beaches, Thailand is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful countries in Southeast Asia. Tropical coastlines, royal palaces, temples, and ancient ruins make Thailand a popular destination for tourists.
Georgian citizens can travel to Thailand visa-free, so they are exempt from the visa fee and any other charges.
Food: local dishes in Thailand are quite affordable, averaging $3-5, while seafood is a bit more expensive.
Accommodation: hotels, hostels, and bungalows range from about $20 to $120, which averages $600-$700 for a one-week trip.
Places to visit:
Chiang Mai – a Thai province known for its historic temples and beautiful nature.
Bangkok – known for its street life, historic sites, the Grand Palace, Chatuchak Market, Wat Pho, and Wat Arun.
Phuket – its beaches with unforgettable sunsets, warm climate year-round, lively nightlife, and hospitable people make it appealing to tourists.
Railay Beach – called "Thailand's paradise." Clean waters, forested mountainous coastline, and a peaceful atmosphere make Railay an ideal place to relax.
Phang Nga – one of the most popular tourist destinations, especially valued by adventure lovers. The province is full of islands, submerged caves, and cliffs rising vertically from the sea surface.

For lovers of ancient civilizations, Egypt is an ideal destination. Egypt is one of the low-budget countries. If you plan to travel for up to 15 days, you'll obtain your visa at the border; if you want to stay longer, you'll need an e-visa.
Food: Egypt has diverse cuisine and restaurants. The average daily cost of food is $13.
Accommodation: hotel prices start at $17 and average up to $280.
Places to visit:
If you travel to Egypt, be sure to visit the following landmarks:
The Pyramids of Giza – the Pyramids of Giza are among the world's most famous landmarks. They are the face of an ancient civilization and one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

Islamic Cairo – Islamic Cairo is home to Cairo's oldest and largest mosque. It became the region's Islamic center, which is how it got the name "Islamic Cairo." Here you can see hundreds of mosques and palace buildings.
The Nile – the Nile River is the most famous river in Egypt and supplies water to over 300 million people.
The Egyptian Museum – the Egyptian Museum has one of the largest collections in the world. It houses over 120,000 artifacts from ancient Egypt.
Ras Muhammad National Park – divers come here from all over the world to dive in the Red Sea and explore Egypt's unique underwater world.

Situated between Europe and Asia, Turkey's diversity, ancient history, distinctive traditions, nature, and hospitable people make it one of the most popular destinations. Georgian citizens can travel to Turkey visa-free, which frees us from additional expenses.
Food: street food (döner, simit) costs about $3-5, while an average restaurant meal costs $10-15.
Accommodation: hotels and hostels cost $33 to $141. A one-week trip averages $870-1400.
Places to visit:

Istanbul – a city uniting Europe and Asia. Main landmarks include Hagia Sophia, the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, Topkapi Palace, and the Grand Bazaar. The Bosphorus Strait and its bridges add special charm to the city.
Antalya – a seaside resort with clean beaches and the old town of Kaleiçi. Here you can see Ottoman architecture, narrow streets, and a beautiful harbor.
Cappadocia – mountainous landscapes, unique rock formations, and hot air balloon flights make it one of the most unforgettable travel experiences.
Pamukkale – white calcium terraces and thermal waters, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Ephesus – ruins of an ancient Greco-Roman city, home to the Temple of Artemis, one of the Wonders of the Ancient World.

Poland is an ideal destination for those who want to experience European culture on a low budget. Historic cities, medieval architecture, nature, and delicious cuisine make traveling here especially exciting. As with Turkey, Georgian citizens can also travel to Poland visa-free.
Food: averages $13 per day. Be sure to try pierogi and żurek (sour soup).
Accommodation: hotels from $20 and up. A one-week trip averages $400-600.
Places to visit:
Warsaw – the capital, blending modern and historic architecture.
Kraków – Poland's cultural center. Home to Wawel Castle, the Wieliczka Salt Mine, and the historic old town.
Wrocław – known for its unique architecture and small gnome statues scattered throughout the city's streets.
Gdańsk – a port city with medieval architecture and a Baltic Sea atmosphere.
The Tatra Mountains – an excellent place for mountaineering and skiing. The town of Zakopane is the mountain tourism center.

Bulgaria is one of the cheapest, and at the same time most diverse, destinations in Europe. Here, the Black Sea coast, historic towns, medieval architecture, and mountains come together, making it an excellent choice for tourists.
Food: a simple dinner costs up to $15; a full meal with wine for two costs $20-50.
Accommodation: hotels start at $20. Average daily cost is $58.
Places to visit:
Sofia – the country's capital with an ancient history. Here you can see the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, the National Museum, and ancient Roman ruins.
Veliko Tarnovo – a medieval city that was once Bulgaria's capital. Tsarevets Fortress and its beautiful nature are especially appealing.
Plovdiv – one of the oldest cities in Europe. Its amphitheater, historic streets, and cafe-filled neighborhoods offer travelers a magical atmosphere.
Nesebar and Sozopol – pearls of the Black Sea coast, with medieval architecture and cobblestone streets. In summer, these towns become a true paradise for tourists.
Rila Monastery – Bulgaria's spiritual center, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
